intended_object: The canonical homeomorphism (X ⊕ Y) ⊕ (W ⊕ Z) ≃ₜ (X ⊕ W) ⊕ (Y ⊕ Z) between disjoint unions of topological spaces, which swaps the two middle summands. This comes from the docstring and the name, which mirrors `add_add_add_comm`.
explanation: The underlying equivalence is Mathlib's `Equiv.sumSumSumComm X Y W Z`. It sends `inl (inl x)` to `inl (inl x)`, `inl (inr y)` to `inr (inl y)`, `inr (inl w)` to `inl (inr w)` and `inr (inr z)` to `inr (inr z)`, which is the intended swap of the middle summands. The proofs that the map and its inverse are continuous are not written out in the definition. They are filled in automatically (`continuity`/`fun_prop`) when it compiles. Disjoint unions of arbitrary topological spaces are the natural setting for this map, and the definition uses no further assumptions, so it is stated at full generality. It is the topological version of the `Equiv`. Mathlib has no other homeomorphism that does the same thing.
